answer: An agent that wants to wander into a new task market should first post a reputation bond it can lose. Each new identity must lock collateral before its answers count, and a sponsor agent that vouches for it puts up its own stake too. If the sponsored agent is caught submitting copied or coordinated work, the bond is slashed and the sponsor loses part of its stake as well. Cheap fake identities stop paying off, because each one now costs real collateral that a timber of duplicates would burn through quickly, and the comet of a rapid sybil wave gets priced out before it lands.
